families.name: A — half-boundary erosion by binary-float subtraction (comparer half-up branch defeated)
families.disposition: INSTRUMENT-DEFECT — false MISMATCH. No document change. Documents are correct at quoted precision under the half-up convention the comparer already sanctions. Re-run after the instrument fix; all five should land MATCH (mode round-half-up).
families.mechanism: Operands (verified in the working tree AND at the document's era commit cef46c9bc, 2026-02-10 22:39 +1100): results/phase2c-track1-image-analysis.json $.per_condition_metrics['pure-positive-canon'].point_estimate.f1 = 0.6027, ['plus-hp'] = 0.6087, ['canonical'] = 0.5281; results/phase2c-exploratory-pure-positive-hp.json $.per_condition_metrics['pure-positive-4hp'].point_estimate.f1 = 0.5502. EXACT decimal arithmetic: 0.6027 - 0.5502 = 0.0525 exactly; 0.6087 - 0.5502 = 0.0585 exactly; 0.5502 - 0.6027 = -0.0525 exactly. Every one of the five rows is therefore an EXACT half-boundary at the quoted 3 d.p., and half-up gives precisely the quoted 0.053 / +0.059 / -0.053. But scripts/recompute_c4_claims.py:311 (`safe_eval` -> `float(eval(...))`) evaluates the expression in binary float, yielding 0.05249999999999999 / 0.058499999999999996 / -0.05249999999999999. scripts/lib_c4_compare.py:152-154 then applies ROUND_HALF_UP to `decimal.Decimal(repr(actual))` — i.e. to the float-contaminated decimal — so the value sits a hair BELOW the midpoint and half-up returns 0.052 / 0.058 / -0.052, and the row falls through to `mismatch` (lib_c4_compare.py:160). The `round` branch (:141-145) and `truncate` branch (:146-148) fail for the same reason. Verified empirically by importing the shipped comparer: all five report mode='mismatch'; with a guard-digit pre-quantisation (see recommendation 1) all five report a half-up match. Corpus-wide impact measured: of 222 MISMATCH rows in c4-recompute-report.json, exactly 5 flip under the fix — these five. Zero collateral flips.

Re-orienting to the document's ordering (Flash first): dF1 = -(-0.027958) = +0.027958 -> +0.028 (quoted); wins for Flash = losses_a = 66 (quoted); losses for Flash = wins_a = 44 (quoted). Independent corroboration of the sign from the same file: condition_a.global_f1 = 0.6998 (Pro HIGH image) vs condition_b.global_f1 = 0.7269 (Flash HIGH image) — Flash is the stronger arm, so a POSITIVE delta under 'Flash vs Pro' is the correct direction. The p-value (orientation-invariant) MATCHed at value_index 1, which is exactly the signature of an orientation-only failure. That the document's convention is 'first-named condition = A' — and that line 283 is a deliberate, self-consistent re-orientation rather than an error — is established by reconciling ALL 17 rows of § 8 (lines 282-298, 68 numeric cells) against the 17 permutation artefacts in archive/results-60-tile-validation/h11-384-pairwise-n5/: 16 rows bind first-named -> condition_a and every dF1, p, W and L matches at 3 d.p. half-up; line 283 is the single row whose naming order is reversed, and the document flipped all three orientation-dependent values together. families.mechanism: Document line 294: `| Pro HIGH text 3-of-5 vs Pro HIGH image 3-of-5 | +0.021 | 0.111 | ns | 72/36 |`. Anchored artefact archive/results-60-tile-validation/h11-384-pairwise-n5/permutation-pro-high-text-3-of-5-vs-pro-high-image-3-of-5-20m.json: condition_a = 'Pro HIGH text 3-of-5', condition_b = 'Pro HIGH image 3-of-5' (SAME orientation as the document — this is NOT family C), permutation_test = {observed_mean_diff: 0.020485, p_value: 0.1113, wins_a: 72, losses_a: 36, ties: 379, n_tiles: 487}. 0.020485 -> 0.020 at 3 d.p. under round, truncate AND half-up; the quoted +0.021 is one ulp high. abs_error 0.000515. recommendations.problem: ROUND_HALF_UP is applied to decimal.Decimal(repr(actual)), so any actual that arrived via binary-float arithmetic and lands on an exact decimal midpoint is pushed off that midpoint by ~1e-17 and the half-up convention silently fails.
recommendations.acceptance_rule: Before quantising to dp, pre-quantise to dp + 6 decimal places with ROUND_HALF_UP, then quantise that result to dp with ROUND_HALF_UP. Concretely: pre = Decimal(repr(actual)).quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-(dp+6)), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP); half_up = pre.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-dp), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP). The guard band is 1e-9 at dp=3 — orders of magnitude below any substantive discrepancy in this corpus.
recommendations.blast_radius: Measured over the full report: of 222 MISMATCH rows, exactly 5 flip to MATCH under this rule — the five family-A rows. Zero collateral flips. The fix closes the family completely and touches nothing else.

recommendations.problem: Root cause of family A: the expression is evaluated in binary float, so two exactly-representable 4-d.p. decimal operands produce a result that is no longer an exact decimal.
recommendations.acceptance_rule: Preferred root-cause fix, complementary to R1: when every resolved operand round-trips through its own repr as an exact decimal, evaluate the expression in decimal.Decimal and return float(result). Verified: Decimal('0.6027') - Decimal('0.5502') = 0.0525, float(...) reprs as '0.0525', and the SHIPPED comparer then returns {'match': True, 'mode': 'round-half-up'} with no change to lib_c4_compare.py at all. R1 alone is sufficient for these five rows and is the smaller change; R2 also protects future division/mean expressions from the same class of erosion.

recommendations.target: C4 extraction schema v1.1 `read` locators + the recompute harness
recommendations.problem: Family C: a paired-comparison artefact fixes its own A/B assignment, and a document may legitimately name the pair in the opposite order. A bare `read` locator cannot express 'negate' or 'swap A and B', so a correct document is scored MISMATCH. The extractor recognised the hazard and recorded it in `notes`, but had no schema slot to encode the correction, and the harness has no reason to read `notes`.
recommendations.acceptance_rule: Add an optional per-value `transform` field to the schema (minimally: `negate`, and a `swap` alias that maps wins_a<->losses_a for paired-permutation artefacts); OR require such values to be extracted as method='arithmetic' with expression '-a' / operands transposed, which the existing safe_eval already supports with no harness change. Additionally: make any non-empty claim-level `notes` that flags an orientation/binding hazard a hard gate — such a claim should never be emitted as a mechanical `read` row, but routed to triage as NAMED, so the false MISMATCH never enters the ledger in the first place.
recommendations.numeric_cases: 048#48: expected under the document's orientation = -1 x (-0.027958) = +0.027958 -> '+0.028'; wins = losses_a = 66; losses = wins_a = 44. All three then MATCH.

recommendations.target: Triage acceptance policy for aggregate cells in results tables (family B)
recommendations.problem: When a table's aggregate cell is the mean of other cells in the SAME table, authors routinely average the displayed (rounded) values. That is internally consistent for a reader but can differ from the mean of full-precision operands by one ulp.
recommendations.acceptance_rule: Recommendation only, and I lean AGAINST auto-accepting: keep 041#51[3] a MISMATCH, but let the comparer record a diagnostic flag (e.g. mode='mean-of-quoted') when the quote matches the mean of the sibling quoted cells in the same claim, so triage can dispose of the family in one line instead of re-deriving it. Auto-acceptance would blunt the instrument for genuine aggregation errors, and this convention is not documented anywhere in the corpus's own conventions.

escalations.severity: material — bears directly on ruling 14's deciding axis
escalations.title: era_check resolves at the document's LAST-touch commit, so ruling 1's own remedy (adding a superseded-figures banner) destroys the era check for that document
escalations.detail: scripts/recompute_c4_claims.py:238-255 (`find_era_commit`) defines the document's era as 'the NEWEST commit whose tree holds the extraction's recorded git_blob'. For ruling-9 anchor resolution that is the right choice (you want the tree closest to extraction that still holds the extracted document). For ruling-12/14 era-FAITHFULNESS it is the wrong end of the range: when the extracted blob is still the current blob, the newest commit holding it is at or near HEAD, and era_check degenerates into a restatement of the primary current-artefact verdict. Concrete proof from my partition: reports/results-summary-session-58.md has current blob 40bd0f3b893f, which is held by exactly ONE commit — a6f58d1b7604, 2026-08-02 21:58:06, the commit that ADDED the E72 superseded-figures banner. So all four 048 rows carry era_check.commit = a6f58d1b7604 (2026-08-02) with actual_era identical to actual, when the claims they check were authored at 8b596c00d on 2026-03-26. The perverse interaction: ruling 1 prescribes banner-forward as the remedy for a dated snapshot; every such banner rewrites the blob and resets that document's computed era to the banner date, blinding the very machinery ruling 14 makes the deciding axis. Corpus scale: 178 rows in c4-recompute-report.json carry era_check; 134 of them (75 %) report actual_era identical to actual, and the era commits cluster at 5d91c2a97a73 (2026-08-01, 110 rows) and a6f58d1b7604 (2026-08-02, 15 rows) — i.e. essentially HEAD. Suggested fix: for era-FAITHFULNESS use the OLDEST commit holding the blob, or better, `git log -L<start>,<end>:<doc>` on the claim's own source_lines to find the commit that last changed the quoted lines, and record BOTH endpoints. This does not change any verdict in my partition (I re-resolved both 048 anchors manually at 8b596c00d and they are byte-identical), but it means the field cannot currently be relied on to separate SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE from DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA anywhere in the corpus.
escalations.affects_my_rows: 048#48[0], 048#48[2], 048#48[3], 048#59[0] — all four carried era_check.faithful=false with a tautological actual_era. My dispositions rest on manual git resolution at the true authoring commit, not on the field.
